display.title: Episode 507: A Time to Be Sad, a Time to Hope (Asarah B'Teves)
display.summary_short: An Asarah B'Teves show: the siege of Yerushalayim and why we remember sad days, a Shema guest, a young member sings Ani Maamin, a poem about davening early, and Ahavas Yisroel.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Asarah B'Teves itself. Uncle Yossi reviews the Hebrew months and explains that there is a time for everything, even a time to be sad, so that we learn from the past and serve Hashem better. On the tenth of Teves, Nevuchadnetzar's army surrounded Yerushalayim; after a long siege the walls were breached on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed on Tisha B'Av. As long as we learn Torah and keep the mitzvos, Hashem, the Guardian of Israel who never sleeps, protects us, and He has promised to turn these sad days into Yomim Tovim when Moshiach comes. A young girl leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. A boy whose parents are from Eretz Yisroel sings Ani Maamin, about waiting every day for Moshiach, and tells what he enjoys about belonging to Tzivos Hashem. The mailbox brings two girls' poem about starting the day with davening. Uncle Yossi closes with the teaching that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred and will be rebuilt through Ahavas Yisroel, then gives candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Remember sad days in order to improve; Torah and mitzvos keep us safe, and Ahavas Yisroel will bring the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash.

date.note: 'Today is the tenth of Teves'; 10 Teves 5752 fell on Tuesday 17 Dec 1991, one week after episode 506. Candles 4:13 fit.
